description: What aidd knows about each test runner, one row for each, in the order `aidd init` lists the runners it finds (by ecosystem). A row's key is the name a command shows the runner by. `not_red_exits` are the exits the runner's own documentation says no test failed in, so a red run that ends with one proves nothing about new behavior. A code the documentation does not give is left out, so an exit nobody documented stays a real failure. `related_tests` is what the documentation says of a mode that runs only the tests related to changed files: with `arguments`, the form `aidd test --changed` suggests for a test command's `related_tests`, and without, why it suggests none. `schemas/languages.json` holds the facts of a language.

not_red_exits.means: an internal error happened while running the tests, or a plugin raised while importing
a command line usage error, such as a plugin that cannot be found or a conftest.py that fails to import
all tests passed but the number of warnings went over the maximum (the runner gives 1 instead when a test failed)

pytest.note: Exit 2 stays a red on purpose. The documentation says the run was interrupted, and the runner also gives it for a collection error, as from importing a module that does not exist yet, which is the usual first red of a new feature on the base commit.

related_tests.means: None built in: the documentation selects tests by path, keyword (`-k`), node id, and marker (`-m`), and names no mode that reads changed files. A plugin, such as pytest-testmon, adds one.

not_red_exits.means: no tests were run or skipped

unittest.note: Exit 1 stays a red: the documentation gives it for the failure of the tests run.

related_tests.means: None built in: the command line selects tests by module, class, method, name pattern (`-k`), and discovery folder, and names no mode that reads changed files.

`vitest related` runs "only tests that cover a list of source files". Vitest watches by default, so `--run` ("Disable watch mode") lets the command end, and `--passWithNoTests` passes "when no tests are found", as for a change no test covers.

`--findRelatedTests` runs "the tests that cover a space separated list of source files that were passed in as arguments", so the files come last. `--passWithNoTests` "allows the test suite to pass when no files are found", as for a change no test covers.
None built in: the command line selects files and tests by glob, `--grep`, `--fgrep`, and `--file`, and `--watch` reruns all tests when a watched file changes.

`--only-changed [ref]` runs "test files that have been changed between 'HEAD' and 'ref'", and since 1.46 the test files that import a changed file too. It compares the commit HEAD, so with a ref it misses a change not yet committed, which `aidd test --changed` reads: aidd suggests none.
None built in: the command line selects examples by file and line, `--example`, `--tag`, and `--pattern`, and `--only-failures` runs the ones that failed last.
None built in: the command line selects tests by `--testsuite`, `--group`, `--covers`, `--uses`, and `--filter`, and names no mode that reads changed files.
None by file: `go test` tests "the packages named by the import paths", such as `./...`. aidd does not map changed files to packages, so it suggests none.
None by file: `-p` tests "only the specified packages". aidd does not map changed files to packages, so it suggests none.

not_red_exits.means: no tests were selected to run, and no other error occurred

cargo nextest.note: Exit 100 (a test failed) and exit 101 (building the tests failed) stay reds: a test that calls code which is not there yet fails to build on the base commit.

related_tests.means: None by file: filtersets select tests by package, and `rdeps()` adds the packages that depend on one. aidd does not map changed files to packages, so it suggests none.

None stable: on Microsoft.Testing.Platform, `--affected-tests` is experimental and needs a separately distributed extension and `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLE_AFFECTED_TESTS=1`, so aidd suggests none while it is emerging. VSTest selects only by `--filter`.
